newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids hold ahead of weather, bears wait.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids hold ahead of weather, bears wait.

text.p: U.S. spot resid prices, helped by forecasts for colder weather next week, held relatively steady Tuesday in lackluster activity, but bearish sentiment was growing amid ample supply and more competitive gas prices.

"Winter is just about over and there's enough inventory to get through February. I don't see any big buying interest," said one cash trader, adding high sulphur, particularly, was well offered after some U.S. Gulf refinery unit outages.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was still pegged on either side of $18 a barrel, with Feb paper steady to lower at $17.60-17.85 and March unchanged at $17.50-75, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also notionally was unchanged at about $19.75, but traders said competitive East Coast city gate gas prices could siphon some utility demand.
High sulphur in New York notionally was steady to down slightly, with three percent now in the high-$15s. Traders said plentiful high sulphur material could pressure the grades further.

At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was still at $16.50 and three percent at $14.25-50. Traders said concerns remained about Star's coker maintenance this month that was cranking out 50,000 barrels per day of extra U.S. Gulf high sulphur.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate swing gas prices were little changed in the low-$3.00/mmBtu area. NYH one percent resid remained at a $2.85/mmBtu equivalent.
